body:
Why scientific institutions are needed

Scientific knowledge develops through observation, questioning, testing and careful interpretation of evidence. Individual scientists contribute to this process, but many scientific problems require instruments, specialised knowledge, trained teams and sustained funding. Universities, research laboratories, government departments and industrial organisations therefore work together to produce and apply scientific knowledge.

Gujarat has institutions concerned with physical sciences, space technology, biotechnology, agriculture, dairy development, forensic science, energy, earthquake studies and industrial research. It also has organisations that communicate science to the public and help researchers convert ideas into useful products.

Scientific research and technological innovation

Scientific research is a systematic investigation intended to produce or test knowledge. Technological innovation involves developing or improving a product, process or service so that it provides practical value.

Basic research seeks to understand natural phenomena. Applied research uses scientific knowledge to address a specific problem. An innovation may emerge from either type of research, but scientific discovery and commercial success are not the same event.

For example, understanding how salts dissolve in water belongs to basic scientific knowledge. Developing a practical method to obtain usable water from a saline source involves applied research. Making that method affordable and suitable for widespread use introduces further technological and organisational challenges.

The scientific method in institutional research

A scientific investigation generally begins with a question. Researchers form a possible explanation, collect observations or measurements, examine the results and revise their explanation when the evidence requires it. A conclusion becomes more reliable when the observations and reasoning can be checked independently.

Measurement is especially important in institutional research. An earthquake research centre may record ground movement; an agricultural university may compare crop growth under different conditions; and an environmental laboratory may measure water quality. The instrument, quantity measured and interpretation differ, but each investigation depends on evidence.

Different institutions perform different functions

Institutional typePrincipal functionIllustrative Gujarat connection
UniversityEducation, training and researchGujarat Technological University
Research laboratoryInvestigation and specialised scientific workPhysical Research Laboratory
Science centrePublic understanding and demonstrationsGujarat Science City
Government scientific councilScience promotion, coordination and supportGUJCOST
Innovation support bodyHelp for inventions, prototypes and startupsNational Innovation Foundation

State institutions and central institutions

An institution's location does not determine which government controls it. A laboratory situated in Gujarat may function under the Government of India, while another institution in the same city may work under the Government of Gujarat. For example, the Physical Research Laboratory in Ahmedabad is associated with the central Department of Space, whereas the Gujarat Council on Science and Technology works under the state Department of Science and Technology.

Some organisations are autonomous. This describes their institutional structure and does not necessarily mean that they operate without government funding or oversight. Similarly, a university may carry out research, but it is not automatically a government regulatory authority.

Prelims focus

  • Basic research mainly develops understanding; applied research addresses identified practical problems.
  • Scientific conclusions depend on observations, measurements and evaluation of evidence.
  • A university, a research laboratory and a science centre have different primary functions.
  • The Physical Research Laboratory is linked to the central Department of Space.
  • Trap: An institution located in Gujarat is not necessarily controlled by the Gujarat government.

[Sources: NCERT, Class 6, Science: Curiosity, Chapter 1, 'The Wonderful World of Science', printed pp. 1–7; Government of Gujarat, Department of Science and Technology, 'Gujarat Council on Science and Technology', Overview and Objectives; Government of India, Physical Research Laboratory, 'History' and institutional information. Official websites consulted 3 November 2026.]

title: Gujarat's Scientific Institutions: Their Purpose and Organisation

body:
Scientific temper and public participation

Scientific development depends not only on laboratories but also on citizens who can observe, question, compare evidence and distinguish verified information from unsupported claims. Scientific temper refers to an attitude that values inquiry, reason and willingness to examine evidence.

Public science institutions make scientific ideas understandable through exhibitions, demonstrations, competitions, lectures and educational activities. Their principal purpose is not to conduct specialised industrial research but to increase scientific awareness and encourage interest in science.

Gujarat Council on Science and Technology

The Gujarat Council on Science and Technology (GUJCOST) is a state-level organisation working under the Department of Science and Technology, Government of Gujarat. It was established in September 1986 as a State Science and Technology Council and became an autonomous registered society on 1 February 2000.

GUJCOST promotes scientific temper, science education, research and development, innovation, intellectual property awareness and scientific capacity building. It also advises the state government on scientific priorities and supports efforts to connect academic research with practical needs.

Regional, district and community science centres

GUJCOST supports science outreach through regional, district and community science centres. Such centres bring practical demonstrations and scientific activities closer to students and the general public, including people who may not have easy access to large laboratories or universities.

The GUJCOST network identifies regional science centres at Bhavnagar, Bhuj, Rajkot and Patan. District and community science initiatives extend the broader purpose of public science education.

Activities may involve observation of natural phenomena, simple scientific models, astronomy awareness, robotics competitions or demonstrations of everyday scientific principles. These activities support classroom learning; they do not replace the specialised research functions of scientific laboratories.

Gujarat Science City, Ahmedabad

Gujarat Science City is a major science education and public engagement complex in Ahmedabad. Its governing organisation, the Gujarat Council of Science City, was registered as a society on 10 August 1999 and works under the state Department of Science and Technology.

Science City uses interactive exhibits, working models, demonstrations and specialised galleries to explain scientific concepts. Its attractions include the Aquatic Gallery, Robotics Gallery, space-related exhibits and other facilities concerned with science and technology. These attractions help visitors understand ideas through direct observation and interaction.

GUJCOST and Science City are distinct

The names are similar, but they refer to different organisations. GUJCOST is the Gujarat Council on Science and Technology, with a broad role in science promotion, research support and policy advice. The Gujarat Council of Science City manages the major public science complex in Ahmedabad. Both work under the state Department of Science and Technology.

FeatureGUJCOSTGujarat Science City
Primary identityState science and technology councilPublic science education complex
Principal roleScience promotion, research support and coordinationInteractive exhibitions and experiential learning
Relevant dateEstablished in September 1986Governing society registered in August 1999

Prelims focus

  • GUJCOST was established in September 1986.
  • GUJCOST became an autonomous registered society on 1 February 2000.
  • Gujarat Science City is located in Ahmedabad.
  • The Gujarat Council of Science City was registered on 10 August 1999.
  • Regional science centres identified by GUJCOST include Bhavnagar, Bhuj, Rajkot and Patan.
  • Trap: GUJCOST and the Gujarat Council of Science City are not the same organisation.

[Sources: Government of Gujarat, Department of Science and Technology, 'Gujarat Council on Science and Technology', Overview, Objectives and Activities; GUJCOST official website, 'Objectives' and 'Regional Science Centre'; Government of Gujarat, Department of Science and Technology, 'Gujarat Council of Science City', Overview; Gujarat Science City official website, visitor attractions and galleries. Consulted 3 November 2026.]

pictures.caption: Interactive exhibits make scientific ideas accessible to students and the public.

title: Science Education and Public Awareness: GUJCOST, Science City and Science Centres

body:
Universities as centres of science and technology

A university contributes to scientific development by educating students, training researchers and conducting academic research. Some universities concentrate on a particular field, while others cover engineering, natural sciences, agriculture, medicine or several disciplines together.

In Gujarat, it is useful to distinguish state universities from institutions established or supported by the central government. The distinction concerns their institutional status, not the importance or quality of their work.

Major technical and scientific institutions

Gujarat Technological University

Gujarat Technological University (GTU) was established in 2007. It is a state university headquartered in Ahmedabad and is associated with technical and professional education, including engineering, pharmacy and management-related fields. It also supports research, entrepreneurship and innovation among students.

Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar

Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar (IIT Gandhinagar) was established in 2008. It is a centrally established institution of national importance, with its campus at Palaj, Gandhinagar. It undertakes education and research in engineering, sciences and interdisciplinary fields.

Sardar Vallabhbhai National Institute of Technology

Sardar Vallabhbhai National Institute of Technology (SVNIT) is located in Surat. The institution began in 1961 as a Regional Engineering College and later became a National Institute of Technology. It is a centrally supported technical institution rather than a Gujarat state university.

InstitutionLocationMain distinction
Gujarat Technological UniversityAhmedabadState technical university
IIT GandhinagarPalaj, GandhinagarCentral institution of national importance
SVNITSuratNational Institute of Technology

Agricultural universities and field research

Agricultural science applies biology, chemistry, soil science and environmental knowledge to farming. Agricultural research examines problems such as crop productivity, plant diseases, soil fertility, irrigation, seed quality and adaptation to local climatic conditions.

Gujarat has several specialised agricultural universities. Their geographical locations are particularly useful for institution-matching questions.

UniversityPrincipal locationBroad academic emphasis
Anand Agricultural UniversityAnandAgriculture and related sciences
Junagadh Agricultural UniversityJunagadhAgriculture, crops and related sciences
Navsari Agricultural UniversityNavsariAgriculture and allied disciplines
Sardarkrushinagar Dantiwada Agricultural UniversitySardarkrushinagarAgriculture and allied disciplines
Kamdhenu UniversityGandhinagarVeterinary, animal and allied sciences

Research and agricultural extension

Research becomes useful to farmers when tested findings reach the field. Agricultural universities therefore combine education and research with extension activities, which communicate tested practices and technical knowledge to farmers and other users.

For example, researchers may investigate whether a crop variety performs well under particular soil and rainfall conditions. Findings from controlled studies and field observations can inform recommendations. A result obtained under one set of conditions should not automatically be treated as suitable for every farming region.

Prelims focus

  • GTU: Ahmedabad; established in 2007.
  • IIT Gandhinagar: established in 2008; campus at Palaj, Gandhinagar.
  • SVNIT: Surat; originally established in 1961.
  • Anand Agricultural University: Anand; Navsari Agricultural University: Navsari.
  • Junagadh Agricultural University: Junagadh; Sardarkrushinagar Dantiwada Agricultural University: Sardarkrushinagar.
  • Trap: IIT Gandhinagar and SVNIT are not Gujarat state universities merely because they are located in Gujarat.

[Sources: Gujarat Technological University, official 'About GTU'; IIT Gandhinagar, official 'About' and campus information; SVNIT Surat, 'About Us'; Indian Council of Agricultural Research, 'State Agricultural Universities', Gujarat entries. Consulted 3 November 2026.]

pictures.alt: Research findings undergo field evaluation with local soil and rainfall considered, then extension brings tested information to farmers for suitable decisions.
pictures.caption: Agricultural research connects scientific findings with practical farming decisions.

title: Universities and Agricultural Research Institutions in Gujarat

body:
Why Gujarat is important in India's space programme

Gujarat, particularly Ahmedabad, has an important place in India's scientific and space-research history. The state hosts institutions involved in fundamental space science, satellite applications and the development of India's private space sector.

These activities must be distinguished. Space science studies physical phenomena and celestial bodies. Space applications use satellites and space-related technology for practical purposes. Space-sector promotion and authorisation concerns the participation and regulation of organisations undertaking space activities.

Physical Research Laboratory

The Physical Research Laboratory (PRL) was founded in 1947 by Dr Vikram A. Sarabhai. It was formally established on 11 November 1947 in Ahmedabad. Its early investigations concerned cosmic rays and the upper atmosphere.

PRL is associated with the Department of Space, Government of India. Its research includes astronomy, astrophysics, planetary science, atmospheric science, earth sciences and theoretical or fundamental physics. It is concerned with discovering and explaining physical phenomena, rather than operating a public science amusement complex or managing private space licences.

Space Applications Centre

The Space Applications Centre (SAC) is a major centre of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) located in Ahmedabad. It was formed in 1972 by bringing together ISRO units working on space applications in Ahmedabad. Its institutional origins include an experimental satellite communication earth station established in 1966.

SAC develops instruments and payloads carried by satellites and works on applications of satellite technology in communication, navigation and remote sensing. Remote sensing means obtaining information about an object or area without making direct physical contact with it, for example through sensors carried on satellites.

Satellite observations can provide information about clouds, land use, water resources, vegetation and environmental changes. The collected data are interpreted to support practical decisions. A satellite instrument and the information obtained from it should not be confused with the launch vehicle that carries the satellite into space.

Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre

The Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) was established by the Government of India on 24 June 2020. Its headquarters is at Bopal, Ahmedabad. The headquarters was inaugurated on 10 June 2022.

IN-SPACe functions under the central Department of Space. Its role is to promote, facilitate and authorise space activities involving non-government entities, including private companies and startups. It provides an institutional route for private participation in India's space sector.

Its primary function is different from that of PRL and SAC. PRL studies scientific questions; SAC develops space applications and associated technology; IN-SPACe enables and oversees participation by non-government space organisations.

InstitutionLocationPrimary function
PRLAhmedabadFundamental physical and space-related research
SACAhmedabadSatellite payloads and applications
IN-SPACeBopal, AhmedabadPromotion and authorisation of non-government space activity

Although all 3 institutions are located in Gujarat, their central institutional links and responsibilities are different. None of these names should be interpreted as identifying Gujarat's principal operational satellite launch site.

Prelims focus

  • PRL was founded in 1947 by Vikram Sarabhai.
  • PRL is associated with the Department of Space.
  • SAC is an ISRO centre at Ahmedabad, formed in 1972.
  • SAC is associated with communication, navigation and remote-sensing applications.
  • IN-SPACe was established on 24 June 2020 and is headquartered at Bopal, Ahmedabad.
  • Trap: IN-SPACe is not the same institution as ISRO's Space Applications Centre.

[Sources: Physical Research Laboratory, official 'History'; Space Applications Centre, ISRO, 'Overview, Genesis and History'; IN-SPACe, official website, 'Milestones' and 'Office Locations', including establishment and headquarters details. Consulted 3 November 2026.]

pictures.caption: Remote sensing converts observations from space into information about conditions on Earth.
